Great food and service
Feb 2026 • Solo
The lounge on the ground floor was busy but not crowded. I started my evening in the restaurant upstairs and chose the Heritage Menu as I was travelling alone and wanted to try a variety of dishes. The quality was excellent and the quantity just right. I also chose the wine pairing which was chosen with care. The service was excellent, with the story behind each dish also explained. The staff spoke excellent English, which helped! Whilst not cheap by Vietnamese standards, I did not think it expensive.
At the end of my meal, which included some surprises that I will not spoil, I went down to the bar to enjoy a drink. In all, a lovely evening!

Not a good choice.
Dec 2024 • Family
Went to Xu after show at Opera house. It was Xmas eve and they were offering a Prix menu along with regular menu. On arrival I made the mistake of visiting the bathroom. As soon as I entered I was crushed with the stench of moth balls. Not a smell but a face slap of toxic odor. That’s pretty much my night. I’m smelled that most ball smell all night in everything I ate or drank. 

Family mostly had prix 4 menu. It was weird. A strange Poke taco to start served over rock for some reason. That way if amy of it ended up on your plate forget about getting it. Second scallops and mushrooms? Scallops were fresh and well done but not sure if button mushrooms would have been my choice. Entree was beef. A very small piece of New York cut that was mostly fat and gristle. 

We left hungry and it took 12 hours to stop smelling moth balls.

Allowed guest to be violent towards a waiter
Aug 2023 • Family
On our last day here in Vietnam, we wanted to go out and eat some good food before heading home. It started well, really nice premises and incredibly sweet waiters. In the middle of the evening, a group came in and one of the men in the group was so drunk that he had forgotten how to behave. He threw the shirt away, went inside and shouted at the servants and his friends. We felt very uncomfortable in the situation, but it helped a little that there were several guards and waiters around us (which actually made the atmosphere worse, that guards were needed in case the man went berserk).
The worst part was that after we had left, my sister told me that the man had grabbed a waiter by the neck and was shouting at him to eat his food, while the waiter's colleague and boss were watching... What the hell? a place that allows people to both create unrest among other guests and treat their employee like garbage?

Good food, but I definitely won't recommend or come again, after that episode.

So good that Xu should be Michelin-Starred
Apr 2017 • Solo
XU Restaurant Lounge is opened by a Vietnamese - Australian Chef named Nguyen Duc Bien, who although Australian, returned to Vietnam and aims to put Ho Chi Minh City on the Michelin-starred map with exquisite menus that are a fusion of traditional Vietnamese and modern cuisine. 

The best way to enjoy Xu Restaurant is to have the shard plates tasting menus. They have 4-course, 5-course and 7-course menus to choose from depending on how hungry you are. Each dish is tastefully curated to highlight the wonderful fresh ingredients of Vietnamese cuisine from different provinces, (North central and south vietnamese cuisines) while elevating the plating and tastes with western ingredients for a more refined taste. 

By Vietnamese standards, this restaurant is pricey, comparable to HK and Singapore prices but when you factor in that some of the Tasting menus comes with Free-flow of Wine if you pay extra, it comes out to only costing about $80 - $100 USD for the tasting menus with wine and that is a good deal. 

The design of the restaurant is tastefully done and modern, however as it is more a romantic restaurant for couples, the lighting is dimmed so that everything has that orange glow and it can be quite dark. 
This dimness is something I have an issue with. 
I understand the rationale in providing mood lighting for romantic couples, but there is still a way to do so in the lighting that the restaurant can be brightened up yet provide a romantic mood for couples. But that is my own personal opinion and perhaps others may disagree. 

Nevertheless the food speaks to itself as to how mouth watering each dish is and how this is one of the best place to dine in Ho Chi Minh City if you feel like splurging on a good meal. It is best to go with a group of friends or with your special significant other. 

My other petpeeve and again, this is my own personal opinion is that unfortunately, the servers are not well-educated on the wines they serve. When you choose the tasting menus, each dish is paired with a good wine. But the servers do not share with you what the wine is nor do they tell you why the wine is paired with the dish. Like for example why is the Chardonnay is paired with the Baby mussels, Beef salad and roasted pork rice noodles? I do not know and the server never explained but the dish itself is delicious. 

Overall i highly recommend going to XU restaurant and Bar for a wonderful night out in Ho Chi MInh City.

The 5 course tasting menu included ALL of the choices - ten small, beautifully presented, fantastic tasting little meals. I have to say, the best taste combination and presentation I've had since Gordon Ramsay at Petrus - seriously, that good. Our biggest problem with the food was that it actually does not have much to do with Vietnamese food as one would expect it. The restaurant calls itself "modern Vietnamese", and that leaves a lot of room for interpretation. For me, the result is more an (unsuccessful) attempt at modifying good Vietnamese dishes by giving them some strange, sometimes western twists. 
The marketing of it all, I have to admit, is excellent. The price for the "product" itself is much too high. 
Out of the 18 different dishes I tasted, only 2 or 3 were really good: the Vietnamese spring rolls (not part of the set menu), the seared tuna with black sesame (tiny portion), and the beef saté on lemongrass. Some of the others were OK, but definitely not worth the price. What I really found bad was that some of the ingredients were of low quality. The king prawn meat was soggy and the pork belly consisted of almost nothing but fat. 
On the positive side, the service was really good and the atmosphere quite nice.

Restaurant staff are attentive, without hovering or making their presence known. As there were so many interesting dishes on the menu, we asked for recommendations and the waiter was happy to assist. The food itself – both traditional and modern Vietnamese – was delicious, as was the wine, which was very reasonably priced given the quality. Even the pace at which the food was brought out was perfect. We were very pleased to be asked each time whether we were ready to have our next dish, rather than have all food brought out to us and shoved down our throats in 30 minutes like most other Asian restaurants we had been to. Our only complaint was the chewiness of the pork belly, which the restaurant Manager was very apologetic for because it was their signature dish. To make it up to us, he very kindly brought us a complementary selection of deserts, which were the perfect finish to our meal. This service was quite unexpected but very much appreciated, as were the other little touches that, for us, placed Xu head and shoulders above the other restaurants that we ate at in Saigon.

We liked the venue, the food, and the service so much that we went back there for dinner two nights later. We were even more surprised to be greeted personally by the restaurant Manager, who remembered our names, as well as the General Manager, who greeted us just as warmly and cleared a large table for us in an intimate corner of the dining area. The General Manager also apologised to us about the pork from our previous meal and organised a complementary selection of entrees for us, which was a great start to the rest of the food that followed. It was yet another fabulous dining experience.

We booked for dinner one more time there, but cancelled at the last minute because we thought that we should venture out and try another place. Now that was a decision that we should not have made. Our remaining two dinners were nowhere near as good, or as memorable. Thank you Xu for your hospitality and service, and for two fabulous evenings out!

Went there for dinner during my maiden trip to HCMC. The decor lived up to its reputation of being chic and modern. Service staff, too, were polite and helpful. But a couple of things convinced me that there is more hype to this place than substance.

Food-wise, really quite a disappointment. The fallacy of restaurants that claim to serve "modern", "fusion" etc food is that mediocre component parts of the fusion can make the sum total exceptional. That is never the case. If East is to meet West, then a truly outstanding outcome can only happen when the East and West elements of cooking are respectively of outstanding standards to start with. Xu fails on this score. The coconut braised pork belly, supposed to be a signature dish, is a good example.

The second thing which spoilt my evening was when I asked for the bill and requested for it to be quoted in US$ as well. A glance at the conversion told me something was not right. The restaurant was using a rate of US$1=VND17,420! I suppose billing/foreign exchange conversion policy is an internal matter for the restaurant. But when other places in the area -- including "fine" places like Caravelle, Park Hyatt, La Cuisine etc -- generally use US$1=VND20,000 (La Cuisine used US$1=VND21,000), I couldn't help but feel that someone was out to fleece me.

Finally, and quite importantly, there was a distinct smell of moth-balls which permeated the restaurant. Far from being "exotic", it made me feel as if I was sitting right next to the toilets!

My favorites were the duck (and i'm not really a fan of duck) and the tempura shrimp (not really a fan of fried food) The whole meal was excellent and we even purchased the menu - it was really unique and available in a actually bound book that included recipes and copies of the day's menu. The cuisine is definitely fusion - this is a far cry from the street food that dominates the country but everything was expertly prepared, hot and flavorful.

Just had dinner at Xu and all I can say - as someone who has eaten fabulous food on 4 continents - is that this restaurant rates among the world's best.

For a price of around $110 USD per person, this gorgeously satisfying meal included very nice wine pairings and a choice from their extensive and exotic cocktail menu before dinner.

The quality of service rivaled the exceptional food, and the modern decor of the restaurant competes with ultra-chic (and far more expensive) restaurants in the USA and Europe.

Bottom line: If you're a foodie and find yourself in Ho Chi Minh City, you must dine at Xu. Clearly, one of the best in Southeast Asia, and on my short list for best ever anywhere.

The bar area, the decor, the music, the atmophere so far was pleasant. My partner and I got escorted up stairs to the dining area. It was a Friday night and was 1/2 full. Mostly Westerners.

We decided to order a few entrees to begin with. There was a lot to choose from and entrees were priced reasonably by international standards. Prices on this menu are cheaper than home.

We had Vietnamese bruschetta, suprisingly pleasant and the ingredients were crisp and fresh. Then we had fresh oysters, pumpkin risottos balls and then prawn and cream cheese wontons. I liked trying out new flavours and I was very impressed. These dishes were cooked to perfection and each dish had its own characteristic and delicate flavours. 

Dishes came out at different times but in a good momentum - it gave my partner and I time to enjoy our conversation and we were able to eat at our own pace.

I couldn't remember what we for mains specifically but my partner and I were able to share both meals. Portion sizes were perfect because we called for dessert!

Another funny suprise - when I looked at the dessert menu their prices were 25000 Dong for each dessert. We ordered 2 to share. A chocolate brownie with icecream and a white chocolate custard. When the desserts came out they each were served on a soup spoon! It was bite size!
Not sure how anyone else would feel about this but I found it amusing and cute! We then ordered 2 more different ones. A pandan pannacotta and a mango with tapoica pearl che - A traditional Vietnamese dessert. They both got served on bite size soup spoons but considering 25000 Dong is only worth just over $2AU I was satisified.
A coffee finished off our evening perfectly and yes, if I were to visit Saigon again I will visit for dinner once more :)

Super trendy & awesome food
My girlfriend and I came here a few years ago when it was new, and we enjoyed it so much we thought we’d come back again on our last night in Saigon. The place was much quieter than we expected – possibly due to what seemed like the explosion of high quality restaurants in Saigon in the last few years – and while we thought booking for a table at 7:30pm on a Friday night would be essential, it turned out we were the only ones in the restaurant when we got there (it did fill up more after the end of the 8pm happy hour at the nearby westerner bars).

The menu seemed to have shrunk a lot since our last visit (which might account for the drop in patronage – with what seemed like less than a dozen dishes to choose from across the whole menu) but we were relieved to find the quality was as strong as ever. Electing to take on the 500,000 VND four-course menu, we were speechless at the quality of the dishes. The re-working of the Caesar salad concept into rice paper rolls was awesome, and something we’re keen to try and do at home ourselves.

In contrast to the meal options, the wine list was extensive, and expensive (but not really more over-priced than any other restaurant in the city). Being a bit budget conscious (and more importantly, knowing how much some of the plonk was selling for back home), we took on an Italian red of a variety we’d never heard of – it was from Sicily, had a ‘D’ in the title, and is highly recommended.

The staff and the service were both absolutely first rate, and the décor and way the place is decked out is also something really really impressive – up there with any of the best, funky restaurants in the world. While the price of the night was pretty high by Saigon standards, we’d have been up for 4 times as much at somewhere like Billy Kwong back in Sydney, and the quality was at least as good, probably better. 

Also, an expat school teacher I spoke to said he always takes friends there when they're in town, and he's been in Saigon for 15 years, so I reckon he knows a thing or two.

Recommend it as somewhere to really dine if you’re looking to splurge.
